video.title: You Can Learn AI Agent Memory Layers | Graph RAG, Vector DB, SQLite, Hermes, Waku

protocol.note: Drafted from the transcript alone, without seeing any jevcut output or other labels.
protocol.times_from: Whisper small transcript; seconds in the source, so labels survive re-transcription

clips.why: Four decisions for maintaining a memory store (add, delete, overwrite, no-op, retire); explains retiring vs deleting with the GitHub-stars example (1,000 stars in 25 days, then 1.3k) and lands on 'these contexts are still important for future tracing' (518.3). Two starts work: the '4 main ways of maintaining a memory system' framing (452.0) or directly at 'Or do we retire some information?' (468.2).

Reflect: merging duplicates and dropping stale memories, tied to Anthropic's 'dreaming' idea of consolidating while the agent is idle; lands on 'a post-mortem or post-process step to maintain the memory system' (584.5).

also_ok.why: How semantic memory gets built: save every turn to a SQLite state.db, consolidate every 5-10 conversations with a cheap auxiliary model, distill facts into memory.md loaded in context. Clear, but harness-specific.

Vector stores: embed words as high-dimensional numbers because computers only process numbers, then similarity search (food near apple, sausages). Clear explanation; leans slightly on 'as I mentioned earlier'.

negatives.why: Repo plug: 1.3k GitHub stars, pip install, 'you will have an agent like this'.
Arena results read off the screen: SQLite 4.6s and correct, mem0 faster, LangMem 7.5s; numbers without standalone meaning.
'Maybe graph memory is overkill, which is why Hermes keeps it simple'; sounds like a take but rests on the Zep demo on screen.
'Zep team, if you're watching, please fix speed'; energetic, but the support is the waiting shown minutes earlier.
